query: How can we reduce declined travel expenses?

per_column.name: is_travel_related
per_column.rationale: The query specifically targets travel expenses, so a flag isolating travel-related rows is a core filtering axis. Values are soundly derivable from short_description/ci (hardware rows correctly marked False).

per_column.name: asset_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing spend into hardware, travel_equipment, cloud_service, etc. gives a genuine grouping axis to distinguish travel vs non-travel spend and see where declines cluster. Categories are well-grounded in the short_description and ci fields.

per_column.name: creation_method
per_column.rationale: Automated vs manual creation is tangential to reducing declined travel expenses; weak analytical leverage for this query. Groundedness is partial: 'automated'/'system_generated' can be read from wording like 'Automated creation', but the manual/automated split for neutral descriptions ('Procurement of new hardware asset' -> manual) is a somewhat unwarranted inference.

per_column.name: expense_source_clarity
per_column.rationale: Largely redundant with is_travel_related/asset_category (explicit_purchase vs explicit_travel restates the same distinction) and adds little new leverage for reducing declines. Values are reasonable readings of the source text.

per_column.name: data_completeness
per_column.rationale: Record-quality flag (missing_source_id, missing_dates) is derivable directly from present/absent fields and could weakly relate to declines if incomplete records get rejected, but it is generic metadata rather than a strong travel-decline axis. Well grounded (nan processed_date -> missing_dates).

per_column.name: requester_approval_pattern
per_column.rationale: Submitter volume could in principle help profile who drives declined travel spend, but the labels are not grounded: the sampled source_text contains no user history or submission counts, yet rows are confidently labeled 'high_volume_submitter'/'first_time_submitter'. This asserts specifics the visible source does not support.

judge.rationale: The strongest columns (is_travel_related, asset_category) directly serve the query and are well grounded, giving real analytical axes for isolating and grouping travel spend. Several others (creation_method, expense_source_clarity) are either tangential or redundant, and requester_approval_pattern makes confident submitter-frequency claims not supported by the visible source text, dragging groundedness down. Judged only on usefulness and groundedness (not completeness), the set is mixed but anchored by two solid columns.
